source.title: Irish News, 10 June 1964, p. 2 ("NOTICE OF RESULT OF ELECTIONS 1964 - COUNTY OF DOWN"); Irish News, 25 May 1964, p. 3 ("Notice of poll, County of Down: Saintfield and Newry Urban")
source.publisher: Irish News (via the Irish Newspaper Archives)
source.check: votes as printed in the Returning Officer's notice: Rogers 1,903, Johnston 924; majority 979. The notice of poll of 25 May 1964 named Johnston and Rogers as the two candidates for Saintfield and Kelly and Mulligan for Newry Urban.

note: Triennial election of Down County Council, polled Thursday 4 June 1964. Saintfield was the only division contested: Herbert Rogers polled 1,903 and John Johnston 924, so Rogers was returned and Johnston was not. The other eighteen divisions were filled without a contest. The Returning Officer's 'Notice of Result of Elections 1964 - County of Down', dated 4 June 1964 and printed in the Irish News of 10 June 1964, p. 2, names the person returned for every division except Newry, where the poll had been countermanded because Mr. F. G. Mulligan (Newry Labour) died between nomination day and polling day; Newry Labour did not renominate (Irish News, 13 June 1964), and the Deputy Returning Officer's notice dated 15 June 1964 declares Thomas Joseph Kelly elected for Newry without a poll (Newry Reporter, 18 June 1964, p. 10; round 2, 7 Nov 2026). The notice prints no party labels, so none are recorded. Only contest of the round. Johnston was the member returned for Saintfield in 1958; Rogers is the candidate who advertised in the Irish News of 3 June 1964 as 'the ratepayers' friend'. Addresses and occupations printed with the names are not reproduced (privacy rule; gap-fill 6 Nov 2026).
